strategies.summary: Use the ITH/ITL hierarchy to decide which short-term highs stay protected while price travels toward the opposing ITL. Once that ITL is swept, expect a deeper retracement into the premium array on the timeframe immediately above the execution chart.

timeframes.notes: Fractal hierarchy. setup_tf is the active structure leg, bias_tf is the timeframe immediately above it via the contract ladder, and entry_tf is the current execution chart; the walkthrough shows daily -> 1h -> 15m -> 1m.

glossary.Draw on liquidity: The immediate target level price is moving toward; in this lesson it is the opposing intermediate-term low during the bearish push, then the higher-timeframe premium array once that low is swept.

custom_signals.name: intermediate_term_high
custom_signals.plain_definition: A swing high flanked by a lower swing high on its left and a lower swing high on its right.

custom_signals.name: intermediate_term_low
custom_signals.plain_definition: A swing low flanked by a higher swing low on its left and a higher swing low on its right.

custom_signals.name: htf_opposing_pd_array
custom_signals.plain_definition: The opposing higher-timeframe premium array (for longs) that acts as the draw on liquidity.

custom_signals.name: overlapping_pd_array
custom_signals.plain_definition: A fair value gap that shares price with another PD array (order block) on the same timeframe; the shared range is the entry zone.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: max(bullish_fvg[0].gap_low, bullish_ob[0].zone_low) <= min(bullish_fvg[0].gap_high, bullish_ob[0].zone_high) AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled AND NOT bullish_ob[0].invalidated

sequence: Mark the active bearish leg with its protected intermediate-term high and its opposing intermediate-term low draw on liquidity.
As price pushes toward that ITL, treat the short-term highs inside the leg as protected unless the larger structure fails first.
When the ITL is swept, expect a deeper retracement rather than immediate continuation.
Project that retracement into the premium array on the timeframe immediately above the execution chart.
Prefer the retracement when multiple PD arrays overlap inside that higher-timeframe premium zone.

invalidation.text: If a protected Intermediate Term High is violated before the target Draw on Liquidity (ITL) is reached, the structure is broken.

filters.text: For the retracement after an ITL is swept, look for multiple PD arrays overlapping (e.g., an FVG overlapping with a mitigation block).

entry_rule.text: After the intermediate-term low is swept, look for the larger retracement into the premium array on the timeframe immediately above the execution chart.
entry_rule.quote: After we take that intermediate term low... retracement into a premium array that is above the one minute time frame.

target_rule.quote: our draw on liquidity is this intermediate term low

stop_rule.text: Place the stop loss beyond the protected intermediate-term high.
stop_rule.quote: this intermediate term high should ideally not get violated at all

presenter_claims.claim: Following this exact step-by-step logic will get you as close to the 'Holy Grail' as possible.
This strategy can yield a 90% win rate (with the caveat that 1 in 10 days will still be bad).

strategies.notes: Framework, not a standalone execution model: it explains when a completed draw on liquidity should lead to a deeper pullback into the next-higher-timeframe PD array. The presenter’s structure is a swing hierarchy (ITH/ITL and protected short-term highs), not Traidle’s BOS/CHoCH bias state machine. The walkthrough is taught on the bearish side even though the idea is symmetric.

confidence.reason: The presenter is extremely explicit about the definitions of ITH/ITL, the sequence of events, and which highs are protected versus targeted.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price sweeps an intermediate term high (which was a previous day high) and rejects heavily, creating a Daily bearish FVG.
Price moves out of the Daily premium array and targets a 1H discount array (an intermediate term low). It creates a series of protected short-term highs along the way.
Zooming in, the price action clearly shows intermediate term highs protecting the downward structure while sweeping intermediate term lows.
After sweeping a local 1m intermediate term low, price pulls back deeply into an overlapping 5m FVG and Mitigation Block. This retracement forms a new protected 1m intermediate term high.

examples.presenter_commentary: The presenter uses this continuous top-down sequence to illustrate the fractal nature of market structure. He emphasizes that predicting deeper retracements becomes highly probable once a Draw on Liquidity (an Intermediate Term Low) is swept, at which point traders should look one timeframe higher for the target premium array.

may_differ.reason: Traidle relies on a standard 3-candle swing point rule. The presenter's ITH/ITL concepts require sequences of multiple swings (a 3-swing fractal), which standard indicator engines do not inherently flag without compound logic.
Custom concept, not an engine detection; moved from should_detect.
